symptom: Starlark parse_xpath('[IsConfidential = false() or Mod.Report_Owner = \'[%CurrentUser%]\']') returned only (IsConfidential = false), with no recovered node and no error; the same constraint with the terms swapped, or with bare false, parsed whole.
file: mdl/exprcheck/parser.go parseIdentLed (true()/false() in XPath mode); mdl/linter/starlark.go builtinParseXPath (E014 → recovered root). Test: mdl/linter/parse_xpath_bool_call_2398_test.go
cause: parseIdentLed returned a BoolLit for true/false before the call check, leaving `()` on the stream; Parse then reported E014 (trailing tokens), which builtinParseXPath discarded with `ast, _ :=`.
insight: **A parser that can stop early must say so to every consumer, not only the one that prints hints.** check printed E014, but the lint builtin threw the hints away, so rules got a partial tree that looked complete — and the truncation depended on term order, the worst kind of false negative for an access-rule rule. Fix both: accept the XPath spelling, and map an error-severity trailing-token hint to the documented `recovered` root.
